newsitem.title: USA: Labor Dept proposes $82,500 fine for NYNEX.
newsitem.headline: Labor Dept proposes $82,500 fine for NYNEX.

text.p: The U.S. Labour Department's Occupational Safety and Health Administration on Wednesday proposed fining telephone company Nynex Corp. $82,500 in connection with the February death of a worker in Lynn, Mass.
The worker, who was not named, was found with severe head injuries lying under an aerial ladder, its bucket door open some 10 feet above him. He later died of his injuries, OSHA said.
"No one witnessed the accident, " OSHA spokesman Ted Fitzgerald said, "but the injuries sustained were consistent with a fall."
Lynn police notified OSHA of the Feb. 5 accident and the agency began its probe.

OSHA found the elevated bucket "had a defective door hinge that was missing rivets and bolts, meaning the door could pop open any time," the agency's area director, K. Frank Gravitt said. "This left the deceased worker -- and any other worker who might happen to use this bucket in this condition -- exposed to potentially fatal falls whenever the bucket was elevated."
OSHA cited Nynex for failing to properly maintain its equipment and for failing to ensure that the worker was wearing a body belt or safety line while working in the bucket.
Nynex spokesman John Johnson said, "We've just received the OSHA citation and we are considering filing an appeal."

Johnson said the company has a contractor that inspects and repairs its vehicles twice a year and that before starting each shift, workers are supposed to inspect and report any problems with their trucks. The 41-year-old long-time Nynex employee failed to do that and he was also not following the company's safety procedures at the time of the accident, Johnson added.
